newsitem.title: UK: Barings bondholders begin action to recoup losses.
newsitem.headline: Barings bondholders begin action to recoup losses.

text.p: A group of investors who bought bonds issued by collapsed British bank Barings began court proceedings on Monday against 17 parties against whom they are claiming 100 million pounds ($167.4 million) compensation.

The High Court writs were issued in May on behalf of the Barings 9-1/4 percent Perpetual Noteholders Action Group on the grounds that the listing particulars of the 1994 issue were misleading or failed to contain certain information as a result of which they have suffered loss. Proceedings have been brought against the issuing company Barings Plc (now under administration) and its board of directors, including chairman Peter Baring, deputy chairman Andrew Tuckey, chief executive Peter Norris and nine others.
Also named on the writ were the managers of the bond issue, Hoare Govett Corporate Finance Ltd, BZW, Cazenove & Co and Baring Brothers & Co (now Bishopscourt (BB & Co) Ltd).
Monday's hearing was not held in open court as parties were involved in legal argument on how best to deal with the litigation, lawyers said.

Barings was rescued by Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep after it collapsed with losses of around $1.4 billion following unauthorised derivatives trades by Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson.
Leeson, 29, is serving a six-and-a-half year jail sentence in Singapore.
